clue.text: Old hat, one side complete

blocks.note: something old hat is out of fashion, or simply out
right is one of the two sides, opposite left

explanation.surface: A worn-out old hat with one side completely gone, or a hat that is complete on one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright as an adjective means total or utter, as in an outright victory, a synonym of complete.

clue.text: For each doorway into work there's puzzlement

to ply is to work at, as in plying a trade
an exit is a doorway out

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a doorway in every workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: Work here is the verb, as in plying a trade, not a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Perplexity is the state of being confused or baffled, a straightforward synonym for puzzlement.

blocks.note: taken as written

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaken up' wants to be the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; the signal is 'appearing reckless' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: About in the sense of approximately is the same as roughly speaking, as in about fifty people.

clue.text: V, a Victory on the way

blocks.note: taken as written
a gain is a win, a victory in a small way

explanation.surface: A V-for-victory sign flashed on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: V is short for versus, as in a fixture listing one team v another.
explanation.definitionFit: Versus, abbreviated V, means in opposition to, which is what against means.

clue.text: Song basso profundo, perhaps, heard?

explanation.definitionFit: A solo is a piece or song performed by a single voice, so it stands for a song here.

clue.text: Cheap American heater?

blocks.note: surface reading: a bargain-price heating appliance bought in the US
setter's reading: a five-cent coin's worth of the great heater in the sky, a phrase that sounds like an actor's surname

explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the themed answers: the phrase sounds like Nicholson, as in Jack Nicholson, one of the ACTORS at 19. A nickel is the US five-cent coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel is cheap American money and the sun is the heater that warms the earth, so the phrase is a cheap American heater.

clue.text: Having no further requirement?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who needs nothing more
setter's reading: something already put to use as much as needed, a phrase that sounds like an actor's surname

explanation.walkthrough: A themed answer: said quickly it sounds like Ustinov, as in Peter Ustinov, one of the ACTORS at 19.
explanation.definitionFit: If a thing has been used enough, there is no further requirement for it, so the phrase fits the question.

clue.text: Cartoon character that gets up your nose, certainly, according to Spooner?

blocks.clueFragment: that gets up your nose, certainly

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure who really irritates you, as Spooner might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets up your nose' is British slang for annoying, but here it is meant literally: a bogy (bogey) is dried snot.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogi Bear is the picnic-basket-stealing cartoon bear created by Hanna-Barbera, an animated character.

clue.text: Political step sees militia leader breaking Alberto Granado's letter opener?

the first letter of militia

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter opener' looks like a paper knife; it is the salutation that opens a letter. Granado was Che Guevara's companion on the journey of The Motorcycle Diaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A démarche is a diplomatic or political move or initiative, formally a step taken by a government.

clue.text: Half-hearted killer, more mature

explanation.surface: A murderer losing enthusiasm, though growing older and wiser.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of RIPPER is its double P; losing half of that leaves one.
explanation.definitionFit: Riper is the comparative of ripe, and ripe fruit or a ripe age is a fully developed one, hence more mature.

clue.text: Duo go off with bike to see travelling companion

indicators.note: something gone off has gone bad or wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair set off on a bicycle tour with a friend for company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling companion' suggests a person, but a guidebook goes with you on the trip too.
explanation.definitionFit: A guidebook is the book tourists carry about on a journey, a companion in the sense of a handbook.

clue.text: A number of noises around tea, say, providing shocks

clue.text: Trophy wife finally left for surgeon's assistant

blocks.note: a scalp is a trophy, once taken from a defeated enemy
the last letter of wife
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trophy wife' reads as one phrase, but trophy and wife do separate jobs. The surgeon's assistant is a tool, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is the small sharp knife a surgeon cuts with, a helper in the sense of an instrument.

clue.text: Sexy melon in image that's pleasant to look at

explanation.surface: An alluring melon in a picture that is easy on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A photogenic person looks attractive in photographs, which loosely means pleasing to the eye.

clue.text: Monster not entirely visible, still

explanation.walkthrough: The final letter is the part out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet and still are synonyms as adverbs meaning even now or nevertheless, as in it is yet to come.

clue.text: Figure dry, missing sherry for a start

a word missing something has that part taken out of it

blocks.note: thirsty means in need of a drink, dry
the first letter of sherry

explanation.definitionFit: Thirty is a number, and figure is a common crossword word for a number.

definitions.note: unclued: the star stands for the theme word linking the five undefined answers

setter's reading: the star marks the theme word, the thing linking the five undefined phrases, each of which sounds like a famous film star's surname

explanation.definitionFit: Ustinov, Gielgud, Gable, Brando and Nicholson are all famous film and stage performers, the group linking the themed answers.
